Indicator 4 tracks the proportion of [[steroidkurer|Steroidkurer]] that are accompanied by a [[dexa-scanning|DEXA-scanning]] to monitor bone density, a critical quality metric managed by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]]. The data compares performance across Danish regions and hospital departments for the periods 2023/24 and 2022/23 [^src1].

Across all measured entities, the national target for this indicator was missed entirely, with every region and department marked as "Nej" (No) for target achievement [^src1]. At the national level, the proportion of steroid courses receiving a DEXA scan was 36% in 2023/24, a slight decrease from 37% in 2022/23 [^src1]. 

Regional trends show mixed performance over the two periods. The Region of Southern Denmark (Syddanmark) demonstrated the most significant improvement, rising from 38% in 2022/23 to 47% in 2023/24 [^src1]. In contrast, the Capital Region (Hovedstaden) saw a notable decline from 39% to 31%, and Region Zealand (Sjælland) dropped from 41% to 37% [^src1]. Midtjylland and Nordjylland remained relatively flat, shifting only slightly to 30% and 34%, respectively [^src1].

At the departmental level, Esbjerg Medicinsk Mave og Tarm Amb. emerged as the leader, achieving the highest proportion at 54% in 2023/24 (up from 48% the previous year) [^src1]. Conversely, Herlev Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd. recorded the lowest proportion among departments with unsuppressed data at 16% (down from 42% in 2022/23), while Rigshospitalet Sygd. i Fordøjelsessystem, C reported 13% but with suppressed patient counts [^src1]. Other notable outliers include Bornholm Medicinsk Afdeling, which jumped from 29% to 56%, and Randers Lever-, Mave- og Tarmsygd., which dropped sharply from 30% to 15% [^src1].
